What To Expect
Overview
Antelope Canyon is one of the world's most famous slit canyons and a popular photographer's spot, located in the northern part of Arizona, USA, near the city of Page, Arizona, which is part of the Navajo Native American Reserve.
The Antelope Canyon is divided topographically into two separate sections. They are called Upper Antelope Canyon and Lower Antelope Canyon.
Upper Antelope Canyon, called in Navajo as "Tse bighanilini", which means "the rock through which water passes", is a wide valley with many visitors. The walls rise about 20 metres high and are about 150 metres long, with only a very thin crack and grey light from a distance.
The whole tour lasts approximately 1 hour and will take you on a guided tour into the Antelope Canyon with a local Navajo guide and professional photographic assistance, using the mobile phone, you will be able to take very nice pictures.

What if you miss the appointed time or departure date?

Once the booking is confirmed, an absence or failure to show up on the scheduled date or time is a no-show. No refunds or reschedules will be issued for no-shows and late arrivals.

Other important information
For bookings starting Jan Dec 31, 2025 the US$15/person Navajo Permit Fee is not included. You will need to pay this fee directly to the Navajo Nation Parks, simply follow the instructions at the Checkin on-site.
Please note the time difference. In winter time, Antelope Canyon time is one hour faster than Las Vegas time; in summer time, Antelope Canyon time is the same as Las Vegas time.
The staff at the ticket exchange supports English communication only.
Please be sure to check in 1 hour before the departure time( excluding queuing time), and 20 minutes before the departure time to stop checkin, late or no show on the day, the tickets will be invalidated without refund
Maintain a distance of 6 (feet) or 1.83 (metres) from others and limit physical contact with people outside the tour group.
Please do not bring tripods, monopods, selfie sticks or any animals on the tour.
Antelope Valley does not provide any animal holding services, so if you must bring a pet or service animal, please consider carefully whether to participate.
Not recommended for pregnant visitors; not recommended for visitors with back problems; not recommended for visitors with heart problems or other serious medical conditions; not wheelchair accessible in the valley.
Visitors as well as children/infants must bring their own car seats and installed in the pick-up vehicle.
